questions.q: State the order of the differential equation $y'' + 3y' - 2y = \sin x$.
questions.answer: Second order (the highest derivative appearing is $y''$).

questions.q: State the order of $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 + xy = 0$, and note that order depends only on the highest derivative, not on any power of it.
questions.answer: First order — the equation involves only $y'$ (cubed), no higher derivative.

questions.q: Verify that $y = e^{2x}$ is a solution of $y' - 2y = 0$.
questions.answer: $y' = 2e^{2x}$, so $y' - 2y = 2e^{2x} - 2e^{2x} = 0$. Yes, it is a solution.

questions.q: Verify that $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$ is a solution of $y' + y^2 = 0$ for $x \neq 0$.
questions.answer: $y' = -\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ and $y^2 = \dfrac{1}{x^2}$, so $y' + y^2 = -\dfrac{1}{x^2} + \dfrac{1}{x^2} = 0$. Yes, it is a solution.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = xy$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = x\,dx$. Integrate: $\ln|y| = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + C$. So $y = Ae^{x^2/2}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^2}{x}$ for $x>0$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y^2} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $-\dfrac{1}{y} = \ln x + C$. So $y = \dfrac{-1}{\ln x + C}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x+1}{y}$.
questions.answer: Separate: $y\,dy = (x+1)\,dx$. Integrate: $\dfrac{y^2}{2} = \dfrac{x^2}{2}+x+C$. So $y^2 = x^2+2x+C_1$ (renaming $2C$ as $C_1$).

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 6x^2y^2$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y^2} = 6x^2\,dx$. Integrate: $-\dfrac{1}{y} = 2x^3+C$. So $y = \dfrac{-1}{2x^3+C}$.

questions.q: Find the equilibrium (constant) solutions of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(3-y)$.
questions.answer: Set $y(3-y)=0$: the equilibrium solutions are $y=0$ and $y=3$.

questions.q: For $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(3-y)$, determine whether $y=0$ and $y=3$ are stable or unstable by checking the sign of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ just above and below each.
questions.answer: For $0<y<3$: $y(3-y)>0$, so solutions increase away from $y=0$ and toward $y=3$. For $y>3$: $y(3-y)<0$, so solutions decrease back toward $y=3$. Hence $y=0$ is unstable and $y=3$ is stable.

questions.q: Find the equilibrium solutions of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (y-2)(y+1)$ and classify each as stable or unstable.
questions.answer: Equilibria: $y=2$ and $y=-1$. For $-1<y<2$, $(y-2)(y+1)<0$, so solutions decrease toward $y=-1$: $y=-1$ is stable. For $y>2$, the product is positive, pushing solutions away: $y=2$ is unstable.

questions.q: Find the general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x$, then find the particular solution satisfying $y(1)=3$.
questions.answer: General solution: $y=x^2+C$ (this one is already separated, with $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ depending only on $x$). Since $y(1)=3$: $1+C=3 \Rightarrow C=2$. Particular solution: $y=x^2+2$.

questions.q: Explain, in terms of the arbitrary constant $C$, why a differential equation typically has infinitely many solutions but an initial value problem typically has exactly one.
questions.answer: Integrating introduces one arbitrary constant $C$, so the general solution is really a one-parameter family of curves, all satisfying the ODE. An initial condition $y(x_0)=y_0$ picks out the single curve in that family passing through $(x_0,y_0)$, which (under standard existence/uniqueness conditions) fixes $C$ to exactly one value.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2y$, $y(0) = 2$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = 3x^2\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = x^3 + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{x^3}$. Since $y(0)=2$, $A=2$: $y = 2e^{x^3}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2xy$, $y(0) = 5$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = -2x\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = -x^2 + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{-x^2}$. Since $y(0)=5$, $A=5$: $y = 5e^{-x^2}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4x^3y$, $y(0) = -3$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = 4x^3\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = x^4+C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{x^4}$. Since $y(0)=-3$, $A=-3$: $y = -3e^{x^4}$.
$\dfrac{dy}{y} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = -\dfrac{x}{2}+C \Rightarrow y=Ae^{-x/2}$. Since $y(0)=8$, $A=8$: $y = 8e^{-x/2}$.

sections.heading: Application: radioactive decay and population growth

questions.q: A radioactive substance decays according to $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -kA$. If $A(0) = 100$ g and $A(5) = 50$ g, find $k$.
questions.answer: $A = 100e^{-kt}$. Then $50 = 100e^{-5k} \Rightarrow e^{-5k} = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow -5k = \ln\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{\ln 2}{5} \approx 0.1386$ per unit time.

questions.q: A population grows according to $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 0.03P$, with $P(0) = 200$. Find $P(10)$.
A bank account earns continuously-compounded interest, $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=0.05A$, with $A(0)=1000$. Find $A(20)$ and the doubling time.
questions.answer: $A(t)=1000e^{0.05t}$, so $A(20)=1000e^{1} \approx 2718.28$. Doubling time solves $e^{0.05t}=2 \Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln 2}{0.05}\approx13.86$ years.

questions.q: Newton's Law of Cooling gives $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_s)$, where $T_s$ is the surroundings' temperature. Separate variables and integrate to find the general solution.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dT}{T-T_s}=-k\,dt$. Integrate: $\ln|T-T_s|=-kt+C$. So $T = T_s + Ae^{-kt}$.

questions.q: A cup of coffee at $90^\circ$C is left in a $20^\circ$C room. If $T(10)=60^\circ$C, find $k$, then find $T(20)$.
questions.answer: $T=20+Ae^{-kt}$; $T(0)=90 \Rightarrow A=70$. $T(10)=60 \Rightarrow 40=70e^{-10k} \Rightarrow k=\dfrac{1}{10}\ln\dfrac{7}{4}\approx0.056$. Then $T(20)=20+70e^{-20k}=20+70\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^2=20+70\cdot\dfrac{16}{49}\approx42.86^\circ$C.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1+y^2}{1+x^2}$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{1+y^2} = \dfrac{dx}{1+x^2}$. Integrate: $\arctan y = \arctan x + C$.

questions.q: Solve $y' = y\cos x$, $y(0) = 1$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = \cos x\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = \sin x + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{\sin x}$. Since $y(0)=1$, $A=1$: $y = e^{\sin x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y}$.
questions.answer: Rewrite $e^{x-y}=e^xe^{-y}$, so $e^y\,dy=e^x\,dx$. Integrate: $e^y = e^x + C$, i.e., $y = \ln(e^x+C)$.

questions.q: Solve $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\ln y$ for $x,y>0$, $y(1)=e$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y\ln y} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$. Integrate (left side is $\int \dfrac{du}{u}$ with $u=\ln y$): $\ln|\ln y| = \ln x + C \Rightarrow \ln y = Ax$. Since $y(1)=e$: $\ln e = A \Rightarrow A=1$. So $\ln y = x$, i.e., $y = e^x$.

questions.q: Determine whether $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y$ is separable. Justify your answer.
questions.answer: No. The right side $x+y$ cannot be factored as (a function of $x$)$\,\times\,$(a function of $y$), since it is a sum, not a product.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\cos x}{y}$, $y(0) = -2$.
questions.answer: Separate: $y\,dy = \cos x\,dx$. Integrate: $\dfrac{y^2}{2} = \sin x + C$. Since $y(0)=-2$: $2 = 0 + C \Rightarrow C=2$, so $y^2 = 2\sin x + 4$. Since $y(0)=-2<0$, take the negative branch: $y = -\sqrt{2\sin x + 4}$.

questions.q: A tank of water drains according to Torricelli's Law, $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -kh^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the water height. Separate variables and integrate.
questions.answer: Separate: $h^{-1/2}\,dh = -k\,dt$. Integrate: $2h^{1/2} = -kt + C$, so $h = \left(\dfrac{C-kt}{2}\right)^2$.

questions.q: For the model $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x}{y}$ with $y(0) = 3$, find the particular solution and state its domain.
questions.answer: Separate: $y\,dy = 2x\,dx \Rightarrow \dfrac{y^2}{2} = x^2+C$. Since $y(0)=3$: $\dfrac{9}{2}=C$, so $y^2 = 4x^2+9$, and since $y(0)=3>0$: $y = \sqrt{4x^2+9}$, defined for all real $x$.
